one_line: A visible human-agent record store for discovering, playing, and curating music.
what_it_does: Lets an agent search and rank a catalog, inspect releases, play previews, manage a reversible crate, and prepare checkout while showing agent and human modes in the interface.
leverage_rationale: Structured catalog, playback, crate, and shared-state tools make agent activity legible and coordinated with the listener; general UI driving could replicate parts but less reliably.
leverage_evidence: About text describes narrow tools for catalog orientation, search/ranking, playback, crate management, and checkout preparation.
Frame sheet visibly shows a central music/record interface, agent panel, and a transition into a distinct agent mode.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent extension of an existing 3D record environment with coordinated agent, player, crate, and detail states, though no video transcript or direct end-to-end proof is supplied.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
Frames show a polished visual interface and agent-mode transition.
impact_rationale: Music discovery and curation have a clear audience, and transparent agent participation can improve exploratory listening without removing listener control.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets listeners and record-curation workflows.
Description emphasizes visible search, consideration, and control transfer.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent record-store metaphor and visible agent presence are a fresh interaction model for music discovery.
creativity_evidence: Concept explicitly places the agent inside the music interface rather than behind it.
Visual agent mode changes the site presentation.
usability_note: Clear human control and multimodal interaction are claimed; dense 3D presentation may add learning cost.
red_flags: Video evidence is absent in the packet metadata despite frame sheets; exact tool invocation is not visible.
standouts: Strong shared-state human/agent music interaction concept.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and originality with a credible, visually coherent product.

one_line: A refund queue where agents propose decisions and humans alone create the applying tool.
what_it_does: Reads policy and refund evidence, drafts approve/deny/partial proposals, stages them for review, and dynamically exposes apply_proposal only after human approval.
leverage_rationale: Tool existence itself expresses the approval boundary, making the human-agent permission model materially more reliable than UI automation or prompt instructions.
leverage_evidence: About text states apply_proposal is registered only while an approved proposal exists.
Shared invoke chokepoint and activity log unify tool and UI mutations.
Screenshot shows refund cards with risk signals and proposed status.
execution_rationale: The core workflow, permission boundary, and adversarial race fixes are described coherently and supported by a populated dashboard, though the packet lacks a video transcript.
execution_evidence: Description reports two rounds of real Chrome adversarial testing and fixes for dynamic registration races.
Frame shows a populated refund approval dashboard.
impact_rationale: Refund operations are repetitive, evidence-heavy, and consequential; this directly reduces drudgery while preserving accountable human approval.
impact_evidence: Workflow handles policy, evidence, reasons, and approval states.
Dashboard visibly includes damage, account, card, and high-value risk indicators.
creativity_rationale: Expressing authorization through the existence of a tool rather than a runtime check is a memorable and deeply integrated interaction idea.
creativity_evidence: Human approval dynamically creates the applying tool.
Project explicitly addresses self-abort and rapid approval/revoke races.
usability_note: Queue cards and visible proposals are understandable; dynamic tool availability may need explanation.
red_flags: No actual video or transcript in packet metadata.
standouts: Permission boundary encoded in tool registration.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and strong operational relevance.

one_line: A detective game where the agent reads evidence but cannot see, forcing genuine human-agent cooperation.
what_it_does: Provides 25 tools for files, mail, messages, photos, browser, terminal, and logs while withholding screenshots and pixel access; the human supplies visual observations.
leverage_rationale: The product is built around complementary human and agent capabilities: structured evidence access for the agent and visual perception for the human, making WebMCP central to the game design.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly withholds screenshot, vision, and pixel tools.
Agent can search/read evidence while human must inspect photographs and describe them.
25 application-specific tools share the game state.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete mystery loop and a consistent rule applied across applications, with a live demo and visual game interface evidence; end-to-end closure is claimed rather than directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: About text specifies the case, evidence sources, correlation gate, and shared service logic.
Demo reported alive with public repository.
Frame sheets show a detective-game workstation/interface.
impact_rationale: As a game it offers credible entertainment and a meaningful cooperative puzzle experience rather than a generic agent demo.
impact_evidence: Clear player-two agent premise and case structure.
Human visual observation is necessary to progress.
creativity_rationale: The asymmetric cognition constraint is highly original and pursued as the central interaction model, not a surface theme.
creativity_evidence: Agent reads every byte but sees none of it.
Case cannot close until human looking and tool correlation both occur.
usability_note: Strongly directed co-op loop, though the many tools and evidence sources may be cognitively demanding.
red_flags: No transcript and no direct visible tool-call proof in packet.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage and creativity with a clear, memorable game concept.

one_line: A voice-operated shared workspace for tour operators and agents to assemble grounded itineraries.
what_it_does: Turns a natural-language trip request into a structured brief, searches inventory, assembles services into a route and timetable, and supports inspection and operational review.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to real inventory and shared itinerary state, avoiding generic itinerary hallucination and enabling precise service linkage.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes structured brief, inventory search, route, timetable, and service-record linkage.
Video is 179 seconds and visibly shows itinerary and detail views.
execution_rationale: The video transcript provides unusually strong end-to-end evidence from request through structured itinerary and service inspection, with coherent operational detail.
execution_evidence: Transcript walks through a five-day Estonia sauna trip and day-level inspection.
Live demo and public repository reported.
Frame sheets show itinerary/dashboard screens.
impact_rationale: Tour operators have a concrete high-detail planning problem, and grounding agent output in supplier inventory can save substantial work while preserving professional review.
impact_evidence: Specific tour-operator audience and complex custom-trip workflow.
Solution combines experiences, lodging, transport, meals, pricing, and route.
creativity_rationale: The shared operational memory layer and voice-to-grounded-itinerary workflow are a fresh synthesis for tourism professionals.
creativity_evidence: Uses unusual sauna-trip request to demonstrate inventory-grounded composition.
Every itinerary item remains connected to an operational service record.
usability_note: Voice and structured day-by-day review fit operators, though the breadth of planning data may be dense.
standouts: Strong domain grounding and operational relevance.
advance_reason: Highly credible, useful workflow with strong video evidence.

one_line: A shopper-controlled WebMCP planner for precise multi-item returns and exchanges.
what_it_does: Reads order and policy data, stages an exact reviewable plan, exposes the same plan on the page, and applies it only after ordinary human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured policy and plan tools reduce ambiguity in conditional commerce actions while keeping approval outside the agent surface.
leverage_evidence: Five explicit tools separate reading, staging, plan inspection, and application.
Early application returns APPROVAL_REQUIRED and repeat application returns duplicate execution.
execution_rationale: The described state machine is coherent and detailed, but visual evidence is thin and no video transcript demonstrates the complete flow.
execution_evidence: Specific fictional order has refund, exchange, keep, drop-off, and totals.
Description specifies not-submitted, approval-required, applied-once states.
Demo reported alive with public repository.
impact_rationale: Returns are a common frustrating workflow, and a precise plain-language plan with shopper control directly addresses accidental or confusing multi-item actions.
impact_evidence: Concrete three-item conditional return/exchange scenario.
Plain-language review and human approval are central.
creativity_rationale: The explicit plan/approval separation is a thoughtful safety-oriented angle on a familiar commerce workflow.
creativity_evidence: Agent cannot approve or reject; ordinary page action is required.
Plan is both tool-readable and visibly rendered for the shopper.
usability_note: Clear review-before-submit model supports accessibility and user confidence.
red_flags: No gallery images and no transcript; frame sheets are the main visual evidence.
standouts: Approval boundary is easy to understand.
advance_reason: Meaningful commerce safety improvement with credible implementation detail.

one_line: A coordinator that computes honest cross-site commitment guarantees before an agent acts.
what_it_does: Reads commitment surfaces from multiple sites, derives the strongest honest guarantee, refuses unsafe combinations, and exposes commit only after human acceptance.
leverage_rationale: It extends WebMCP with reversibility semantics and uses dynamic tool registration to make impossible or unapproved commitments unavailable, solving a coordination problem UI driving cannot reliably solve.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows read-only tools, absent commit tool, human acceptance registering it, and abort removal at commitment start.
Convention models reservable, compensable, and irreversible actions.
Refuses plans with two irreversible actions.
execution_rationale: The video gives a coherent demonstrated workflow, safety states, and 14 signed receipt cases including audit findings and cross-origin verification.
execution_evidence: 116-second video transcript explicitly walks through accept/register, refusal, receipt, and audit flows.
Frame sheets show the coordinator interface and receipt/audit views.
Live demo and public repository reported.
impact_rationale: Cross-site booking failures and false assurances are real high-cost problems; honest guarantees and refusal can prevent consequential user harm.
impact_evidence: Concrete flight/hotel/visa scenarios.
Signed counterparty receipts and atomicity refusal address trust and reversibility.
creativity_rationale: The commitment-surface convention and agent that cannot overpromise are unusually original, ambitious, and coherently pursued.
creativity_evidence: Reversibility is elevated to a first-class WebMCP contract.
Permission model combines tool registration, abort control, and independent receipts.
usability_note: The guarantee-first interaction is clear conceptually; cross-site commitment semantics may require onboarding.
standouts: Strongest evidence packet in the set.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage, high impact, and unusually complete evidence.

one_line: A local-first redaction editor with privacy-filtered agent assistance.
what_it_does: Opens PDFs/images locally, detects likely sensitive content, manages editable masks, verifies export safety, and leaves final download/share to a human.
leverage_rationale: Structured mask metadata and privacy-filtered tools let an agent assist with a visual redaction workflow without receiving document contents, while human export remains protected.
leverage_evidence: Nine narrow tools expose summaries, mask metadata, focus, generic signals, edits, undo, and safety checks.
Agent cannot download or share the file.
execution_rationale: The workflow and privacy contract are coherent and scoped, but there is no video or gallery evidence beyond frame sheets and the packet does not demonstrate export end to end.
execution_evidence: Description covers opening, detection, editing, flattening, and human share flow.
Demo reported alive with public repository.
impact_rationale: People handling sensitive documents have a real privacy problem, and local processing plus non-disclosing agent assistance directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Avoids uploading sensitive files and excludes document text/values from tool responses.
Supports PDFs and images with permanent flattened output.
creativity_rationale: The narrow privacy-preserving contract and shared visual mask state are a strong original angle on document redaction.
creativity_evidence: Agent assists without seeing private document content.
Human remains sole actor for download/share.
usability_note: Editable masks, preview opacity, and local-first behavior support careful review; visual redaction still demands user attention.
red_flags: No gallery images and no transcript; end-to-end export is not visibly proven.
standouts: Useful human/agent division for visual decisions.
advance_reason: Strong privacy-focused workflow and meaningful WebMCP delta despite limited visual proof.

leverage_rationale: Structured college facts and visual comparison improve research organization, but a general agent could achieve much of the same outcome with more friction.

one_line: A shared economic laboratory where humans and agents investigate and test a visible simulated country.
what_it_does: Lets users inspect metrics and regions, change policies, trigger shocks, advance time, query causal history, and run isolated counterfactual timelines without overwriting live state.
leverage_rationale: Semantic domain tools, shared live state, causal history, and isolated counterfactual replay create precision and repeatability that generic UI driving would struggle to match.
leverage_evidence: 17 tools expose exact state, regions, sectors, histories, policy/event changes, counterfactuals, and visible focus.
Flagship workflow compares flood and no-flood timelines while preserving the live country.
execution_rationale: The deterministic simulation and live-versus-alternate timeline model are coherent and ambitious, with a clear domain workflow; direct end-to-end visual proof is limited.
execution_evidence: Description specifies causal chain tracing and isolated replay semantics.
Live demo and public repository reported.
Frame sheets reportedly show simulation/map and inspector views.
impact_rationale: It offers credible value for economics learning, policy experimentation, and explainable causal reasoning in a safe simulation.
impact_evidence: Users can manipulate rates, taxes, spending, tariffs, and shocks.
Counterfactuals preserve live state and make claims testable.
creativity_rationale: The shared visible country plus causal-history and alternate-timeline interaction is an ambitious, memorable use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent investigate the same semantic simulation.
Counterfactual replay removes one event while preserving later interventions.
usability_note: The inspector and scenario comparison support learning, but economic state and causal history may be complex.
red_flags: No video transcript and only one gallery image; visual proof of full counterfactual flow is limited.
standouts: Excellent semantic state and counterfactual design.
Strong fit for explainable human-agent investigation.
advance_reason: High-leverage educational simulation with ambitious shared-state experimentation.
